name: Hindu Control to Triangle
summary: The bottom Hindu Control holder uses the taught kick-through response to establish a leg triangle around the neck and one arm, stopping at control before a separate finish.
description: The bottom Hindu Control holder uses the taught kick-through response to establish a leg triangle around the neck and one arm, stopping at control before a separate finish.
overview:
The bottom Hindu Control holder uses the taught kick-through response to establish a leg triangle around the neck and one arm, stopping at control before a separate finish.

Begin as the bottom Hindu Control holder with the leg-in head enclosure established. Remove finishing pressure before changing the head-and-leg arrangement.

Support the raised knee through the hip angle as the enclosure changes. Use the taught kick-through response to bring the leg into the triangle-control arrangement. Establish the leg triangle around the neck and one arm as Triangle Control/Bottom. Stop at the control checkpoint; a submission finish requires its own separate action.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Hindu Control to Triangle Defender
defender.description: Recognize Hindu Control to Triangle and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Recognize the leg exchange before the triangle closes. Maintain head and shoulder alignment while space remains. Keep the arm near the torso before the enclosure isolates it. Tap if the neck is loaded instead of forcing the exchange. Recognize ordinary closed guard if the high-leg control fully releases.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

flashcards.answer: Recognize the leg exchange before the triangle closes.

flashcards.question: Against Hindu Control to Triangle, when must you stop moving?
flashcards.answer: Stop at a tap, verbal signal, distress, or a loaded joint or neck. Release before changing direction.

flashcards.question: Against Hindu Control to Triangle, does interrupting one grip guarantee a new position?
flashcards.answer: No. Confirm the remaining body and leg controls before claiming the guard, pin, or submission has changed.
